history.summary: 11th-century twin temples inside the Gwalior Fort, built between 1090 and 1093 CE by King Mahipala of the Kachchhapaghata dynasty. The larger temple (Saas) is dedicated to Aniruddha, an avatar of Vishnu (Krishna's grandson), built for the king's Vaishnava queen; the smaller (Bahu) is dedicated to Shiva, built for his daughter-in-law, a Shiva devotee - an inscription decoded by Alexander Cunningham records this. 'Sahastrabahu' (the thousand-armed one, an epithet of Vishnu) was shortened to 'Sas-Bahu' locally. The temples are Nagara/Bhumija style, once three-storeyed; the tower and sanctum were destroyed in medieval invasions, and the surviving entrance porch and mandapa are a protected ASI monument. Not an active worship site today; no festival calendar.

name: Sahastrabahu Temple (Saas-Bahu Ka Mandir)
town_description: Gwalior is a historic city in northern Madhya Pradesh, dominated by the massive hilltop Gwalior Fort. Ruled by the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Kachchhapaghatas, Tomars, Mughals, Marathas and finally the Scindias, it is famed for its palaces, temples and Jain rock-cut sculptures. Gwalior is also a major centre of Hindustani classical music and the home of the Gwalior gharana.
